 PBKS release six players including Ferguson, Owen; Stoinis retained
 Bharat Sharma 
 17 November, 2026 05:49 pm IST

 New Delhi, Nov 17 (PTI) New Zealand pacer Lockie Ferguson and Australia all-rounder Mitchell Owen were among the six players released by the Punjab Kings ahead of the IPL player retention deadline on Tuesday.
 The most notable Indian player released was Nehal Wadhera, whereas Pyla Avinash, Visual Nishad, and Parvin Dubey are the other players let go by the franchise.
 After due deliberation, the franchise decided to retain Australian all-rounder Marcus Stoinis despite the abundance of all-rounders in their roster, which was bolstered several folds after Hardik Pandya joined their ranks following a high-profile trade with Mumbai Indians.
 Show Full Article
 The other all-rounders in the side are South Africa’s Marco Jansen and Afghanistan’s Azmatullah Omarzai.
 After letting go of Arshdeep Singh in exchange for Pandya, PBKS will look to bolster their bowling at the auction next month.
 “The team has decided to release six players. Stoinis has been retained as he continues to be backed by the team management under head coach Ricky Ponting. The squad will be lighter compared to last year.
 “There is little point in carrying too many players who are not going to get a game. It becomes tough for them also,” an IPL source said.
 Ferguson played three games for the franchise in 2026, conceding 141 runs off 66 balls. The bowlers let PBKS down in the second half of the 2026 edition, costing them a play-off berth following a sensational first half.
 While Owen did not play last season, Wadhera took part in eight games, tallying only 65 runs at a strike rate of 114.04.
 Avinash and Nishad are yet to make their IPL debuts, while Dubey got just one game last season.
 Apart from Stoinis, the Australian players who have been retained by PBKS include Cooper Connolly, Ben Dwarshuis, and Xavier Bartlett. PTI BS DDV
